name: Refugio antiaéreo del Ayuntamiento, Valencia
story: From November 1936 to October 1937, Valencia was the seat of the Republican government, and it became a target. The first air raid came on 12 January 1937, and Italian bombers from Mallorca carried out most of the attacks that followed. The city dug more than 50 public shelters and adapted about 200 basements. In 1938 the architect José Luis Testor built this school shelter under the former Casa de la Enseñanza, next to the Town Hall, for 700 children. Five parallel vaulted chambers had ventilation, lighting and latrines. The Town Hall itself was bombed on 28 May 1937. The shelter was restored in 2016 and opened in 2017.
see: Five barrel-vaulted concrete chambers with original benches, restored signage, and panels on the bombing of Valencia and its shelter network.
plan: Free, self-guided entry through the Town Hall exhibition hall at Calle Arzobispo Mayoral 1, Tuesday–Sunday; closed Mondays. Bring photo ID.

boxes.text: Totals for the bombing of Valencia vary. Tourism Valencia gives more than 440 raids, about 800 dead and 3,000 wounded; other counts differ.
